minutes.headline: Library trustees unanimously approved updated bylaws, with wording changes, to go to the town manager for review.
minutes.summary: The Library Board of Trustees approved three sets of prior minutes, heard the director's monthly report including FY22 spending and the FY23 budget request, and reviewed Chapter 7 of the trustee handbook on funding. The main business was a line-by-line review of new bylaws, amended on advocacy and ex-officio wording, then approved by roll call. A friends-group update followed before adjournment.

Accept the January 20 minutes as amended
Accept the February 2, 2022 special meeting minutes as amended

votes.outcome: roll call taken; yes votes heard from Laura, Bob, Dick, Kate, Donna, Maya and Michael Ray; full count not clearly stated

budget_items.what_was_said: Salaries and utility lines (electricity, heating) moved up since last month; the budget is about two thirds through the year and roughly 56 percent expended.

The director met with the town manager and the finance committee head, and will present to the full finance committee. The request includes added hours and shifting expenses from the Friends to the town budget.

budget_items.topic: FY23 request versus town manager target
budget_items.what_was_said: Last year's request was only slightly above the town manager's target; this year's request is above it by roughly twelve percent.
A draft LSTA grant for STEM kits and repair clinics has gone to a consultant, with the final draft due in April.
Replacing the remaining thin client public computers needs funding sources to be identified.
State aid has been fairly consistent in recent years.
The director described Friends funds, municipal support, state aid, gifts and memorials, grants, and service club donations as funding sources.
The Friends discussed electronic membership and donations, accepting card processing costs, and Amazon Smile to raise funds.

decisions.decision: The director will take the approved bylaws to the town manager on the 28th, verify the General Laws citations, and incorporate the edits.
Advocacy clause reworded to support legislation benefiting the Lunenburg library as well as the greatest good for the greatest number of libraries.
Chair duty changed from serving as ex-officio member of each committee to may serve.
The italicized vacancy phrase will be dropped because the charter already covers it.

what_happened.line: Library trustees approved the updated bylaws as amended, by unanimous roll call, for the director to take to the town manager.
Amendments reworded the advocacy clause and changed the chair from serving as ex-officio member of each committee to "may serve."
The director said the FY23 library request is above the town manager's target and includes added hours and moving some expenses from the Friends to the town budget.
The director reported FY22 library spending about two thirds through the year, with salary and utility lines up since last month.
Trustees approved three sets of prior minutes and reviewed the handbook chapter on library funding sources.

why_it_matters: The FY23 library request asks the town budget to carry costs the Friends group now pays, so residents may be asked to weigh it against the town manager's target at budget time.
The bylaws govern how the library board operates, and they still need town manager review before they are final.
